page.overview:
What is Autódromo José Carlos Pace?

Autódromo José Carlos Pace, also known by its former name Interlagos, is a circuit located in São Paulo, Brazil. It was renamed after Carlos Pace, the Brazilian driver who died in a 1977 plane crash. It is the current home of the Brazilian Grand Prix.

The land on which the circuit is located was originally bought in 1926 by property developers who wanted to build housing. Following the 1929 stock market crash, the housing project was suspended, and it was eventually decided to build a racing circuit instead.

Construction started in 1938 and the track was inaugurated in May 1940.

The traditional name of the circuit (literally, "between the lakes") comes from the fact that it was built in a region between two large artificial lakes, Guarapiranga and Billings, which were built in the early 20th century to supply the city with water and electric power. Formula One started racing there in 1972, the first year being the required "dry run" non-championship race. It was won by Argentinean Carlos Reutemann. The first World Championship Brazilian Grand Prix was held at Interlagos in 1973, and was won by defending Formula One World Champion and local hero Emerson Fittipaldi. Fittipaldi won the race again the following year in bad weather, and Brazilian driver José Carlos Pace won his only race at Interlagos in 1975.
